DecisionPoint seeks an AI/ML Engineer to rapidly develop prototypes, implement integrations, and operationalize AI/ML capabilities that support a large federal and DoD-aligned mission environment. This role builds fast proofs-of-concept, API-based integrations, and lightweight user-facing components that validate new AI/ML ideas and help transition successful models into production dashboards and applications.
The AI/ML Engineer collaborates closely with data scientists, dashboard teams, developers, and PMO leadership to ensure AI/ML models are usable, optimized, and appropriately embedded into mission workflows.
This position is fully remote.
Duties & Responsibilities
The AI/ML Engineer will:

• Develop rapid prototypes, microservices, APIs, widgets, and integrations to validate new AI/ML concepts.

• Integrate ML models into dashboards, applications, and operational workflows.

• Build lightweight UI components that demonstrate how AI outputs can be consumed.

• Optimize ML pipelines for performance, scalability, and efficient inference.

• Collaborate with AI/ML Architects and Data Scientists to operationalize models and automation logic.

• Build API wrappers, routing logic, and connector services for ML model interactions.

• Validate prototype functionality, performance, error handling, and model integration.

• Contribute to documentation of models, prototypes, integrations, and deployment patterns.

• Recommend improvements based on usability testing, technical feedback, and mission needs.

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning, Statistics, or a related field.

• Minimum 5 years of experience in software development, AI/ML engineering, or data-driven application development.

• Experience building API-driven prototypes, integrations, or microservices.

• Experience integrating ML models into dashboards, applications, or mission workflows.

• Experience working with data scientists or ML engineers to transition models to production.
Technical Knowledge (Required)

• Proficiency with Python, JavaScript, or similar development languages.

• Familiarity with ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-Learn).

• Experience building REST APIs, web services, or integration layers.

• Understanding of data pipelines, preprocessing steps, and ML lifecycle workflows.

title: Quality Assurance & Standards Manager
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join: 

Every day, Airbnb hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. Since our founding, more than 5 million hosts have welcomed over 1.5 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Airbnb Experiences are completely reimagined experiences, hosted by local people, brands, businesses and content creators who know their city best. Every activity offers guests an authentic way to connect with the place they're in and to meet people with shared interests.

Fraud & Safety Delivery (FSD) is at the heart of keeping Airbnb safe for the millions of hosts and guests who trust our platform every day. As part of Global Operations, FSD investigates and enforces on fraud and safety cases across the full user lifecycle, from account creation to post-stay, leveraging a team of internal and partner specialists operating 24/7 across the globe. We're entering a new chapter: building AI-native, self-service operational infrastructure that lets our teams move faster, make better decisions, and focus their energy where it matters most.

This role sits within Scaled Services, the team that owns the foundational capabilities the entire FSD organization depends on: how we launch, how we measure quality, how we build tools, and how we use data.

The Difference You Will Make:

Fraud and Safety Delivery is judgment work at scale. Our specialists weigh incomplete evidence and make consequential calls about accounts, listings, and bookings thousands of times a day, across many risk domains across the globe. Precision matters in both directions: a missed signal puts our community at risk, and an incorrect enforcement affects someone's livelihood or their travel plans.

As the Senior Program Manager, Quality Assurance & Standards, you'll build FSD's quality program, not an audit function that scores specialists against a checklist, but a measurement system that tells the organization how accurate its decisions are, where quality breaks down, and what to change. You'll design and stand up that framework while running the quality reviews the organization depends on today, reporting to the Senior Manager, Scaled Services.

You'll own three outcomes for the org:

• A quality framework we can defend: One documented model that measures both workflow adherence and decision quality, with published standards, thresholds, and severity definitions across every risk domain.

• Objective, centralized governance: Serve as the impartial quality authority across FSD, setting consistent standards that hold up across domains, sites, and geographies.

• Measurable improvement in decision accuracy: Fewer incorrect enforcement outcomes, diagnosed at root cause and fixed at the source, without adding cost or handling time to the operation.

A Typical Day: 

Set the direction for quality

• Own the quality program end to end, including quality delivery through our partner sites.

• Set the strategy and operating rhythm for how the quality program delivers against FSD's roadmap and goals.

• Represent quality in FSD leadership forums, and build credibility with the teams whose work you measure.

Build the quality framework and standards

• Design a two-layer quality model that measures both workflow adherence and the accuracy of the enforcement decision.

• Establish how we determine the correct outcome for judgment-based decisions, through expert review panels, blind double-review, and a library of benchmark cases.

• Build a severity-weighted error taxonomy and a risk-weighted samp

Early-career professionals including undergraduate/graduate/law students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Successful candidates will interview with both our non-profit partner organizations and Stand Together Fellowships staff, so we strongly encourage you to begin the admissions process early!

About Competitive Enterprise Institute:
 
The Competitive Enterprise Institute is a nonprofit think tank based in Washington which focuses on critical economic and regulatory policy issues.
 
CEI’s internship program provides interested students and recent graduates the opportunity to learn about and promote the principles of limited government, free enterprise, and individual liberty. A CEI internship gives applicants the opportunity to work alongside some of the most prominent regulatory affairs scholars and policy specialists.
 
CEI offers a number of internships across the various policy areas we work on, as well as internships in communications and marketing. Generally, CEI’s policy interns are assigned to work with a specific CEI expert for the duration of their internship; and our communications and marketing interns work with the CEI staff of each respective team.

There may be opportunities for policy research and writing as well. 
 
Qualifications:
Applicants must have a strong interest in policy and politics, capitalism and economics, and libertarian/conservative principles. Applicants must have strong research, writing, and organizational skills. Applicants must possess a professional demeanor and the ability to handle confidential and private information. Applicants should be able to work independently, effectively, and efficiently. A basic understanding of Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook is a must.
 
CEI also seeks interns to work on policy/research, marketing - and from time to time, philanthropy/fundraising, government affairs, events, litigation, and IT. During the interview, we would be more than happy to discuss these other opportunities if they are available and of interest to you!

title: Security Operations Engineer

Working within DeepHealth 's established security frameworks and under the direction of the Director, Security Operations, this position operates and tunes security controls, detection content, and guardrails. Independent validation of those controls sits with the security operations watch function - a deliberate separation that keeps the control environment defensible under audit. Remediation follows system ownership across Cloud Operations, Platform, and Application Development; this role supplies technical guidance and implements fixes directly where the control is security-owned.
This position operates within a regulated healthcare environment across a global operating footprint, with obligations under HIPAA, ISO/IEC 27001, and SOC 2. The role reports to the Director, Security Operations, with future reporting to the Manager, Security Operations as that position is established.
Requirements

• Implement and maintain least-privilege access models, roles, and policies across multiple cloud identity systems.

• Implement container and Kubernetes security controls, including role-based access control, workload security standards, image scanning, and runtime protection.

• Implement and maintain secrets management practices and tooling, and support the elimination of hard-coded credentials across environments.

• Operate vulnerability management tooling, validate scan coverage, and translate raw scanner output into prioritized, owner-routed findings.

• Provide technical remediation guidance to cloud, platform, identity, application, and endpoint owners, who retain accountability for closure of findings in their systems.

• Implement engineering fixes for findings that fall to security-owned tooling and configuration.

• Support remediation tracking for penetration test and vulnerability assessment findings by supplying technical detail and validating that fixes are technically sound.

• Support incident detection and response through hands-on technical investigation, including log analysis, endpoint examination,

title: Process Engineer
description:

We believe the world needs a better food system: more sustainable, more inclusive, and bringing healthier, more personalised food to everyone. In every city we operate, we handpick the best and freshest local produce - from butchers to bakeries - and work directly with farmers through our Farm-to-Door program, alongside the trusted brands and affordable own-label products our customers love.

The Automation team designs and implements the innovative processes, equipment and automation solutions that shape Rohlik's fulfillment network. Working closely with local and central teams, we drive scalability, efficiency and innovation across every part of our operations.

 

THE ROLE

As a Process Engineer, you'll own end-to-end improvement projects across our fulfillment network - from spotting a process that's slow, costly or manual, to delivering a live, working solution on the warehouse floor. Your projects will span both hardware (robotics, automated material handling, conveyor and packing systems) and software (control logic and orchestration optimisation), using whichever combination best solves the problem.

- Feed insights from delivered projects into the group automation roadmap and warehouse planning concepts

As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

The Program Integration Analyst supports critical decisions, strategic intent, and the flow of dependent actions across the major pillars of Anduril's Dive-XL organization. The role exists to:

You’re the person teams call when Postgres is misbehaving in production. You understand what’s happening under the hood, from MVCC and autovacuum to the planner and WAL, and you can turn that understanding into configuration and maintenance changes that keep systems healthy. You’re calm during incidents, rigorous in root cause analysis, and confident communicating findings and recommendations to both engineers and stakeholders.
You’ll excel in this role at Bitovi if you have:

• Deep, production experience administering PostgreSQL on self-managed, on-premise infrastructure (not only managed services like RDS or Cloud SQL)

• Expert knowledge of vacuum and autovacuum: tuning thresholds and cost limits, diagnosing and remediating table and index bloat, and preventing transaction ID wraparound

• Strong indexing expertise: choosing among B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, partial, and covering indexes, identifying missing, unused, and duplicate indexes, and rebuilding indexes safely in production

• Experience with replication and high availability (streaming and logical replication, Patroni, repmgr, or similar) and failover testing

• Backup, restore, and point-in-time recovery experience (pgBackRest, Barman, or similar), including regular restore validation

• Connection pooling with PgBouncer or Pgpool-II

• Monitoring and alerting for Postgres (Prometheus postgres_exporter, pgwatch, Datadog, or similar) focused on catching problems before they become outages

• Solid Linux administration skills as they relate to database hosts: storage, filesystems, kernel parameters, and resource contention

• Incident response and root cause analysis experience, including writing clear postmortems and remediation plans

Other skills we value

• Configuration management for database fleets (Ansible or similar) so settings are consistent, reviewed, and repeatable

• Writing runbooks and maintenance procedures that client teams can own after an engagement

• Capacity planning and performance baselining

• Major version upgrades and schema migrations with minimal downtime

• Working within change management processes in large, regulated enterprises

• Security hardening: roles and privileges, pg_hba configuration, TLS, and auditing (pgAudit)

• Running Postgres on Kubernetes (CloudNativePG, Crunchy Postgres Operator, or similar)

• Scripting and automation in Python, Bash, or Go

• Experience with other relational databases (Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL)

title: Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) - Brookline, MA
description:
Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) $70 K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth , we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

• Starting Salary range: $70,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year.

• 401K with maximum employee matching.

• Health care benefits.

• Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.

• Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.

• Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

• Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.

• Customized schedules within available clinic hours.

• Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).

• Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.

• Incredible administrative support team.

• Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.

title: Plumbing Engineer, R&D
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

THE MECHANICAL ENGINEERING TEAM

You'll join the mechanical engineers in Fluidstack's infrastructure R&D group, who design the cooling, water, and fire systems inside gigawatt-scale AI data centers as repeatable products rather than one-off site designs. Liquid-cooled compute makes water a primary utility: make-up water, treatment, condenser and process loops, and drainage all have to be sized, specified, and standardized so the same design ships to every site.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- Standardizing the domestic, process, and make-up water systems that feed liquid cooling plants so they can be ordered as kits and installed in prefabricated modules.

- Sizing water supply, storage, and drainage for cooling loads that swing faster than conventional plumbing design assumes.

- Coordinating water treatment, backflow protection, and chemical dosing with the controls and water-quality engineers who operate the loops.

- Turning field and commissioning findings into design changes that reach the next site.

ROLE SCOPE

- Own the plumbing design. Design domestic water, process and make-up water, condenser water piping, drainage, and stormwater systems for data center buildings and prefabricated modules, from concept through construction documents.

- Size and specify. Run hydraulic calculations, select pumps, valves, backflow preventers, water heaters, and storage, and write the specifications vendors and contractors build to.

- Hold the codes. Keep designs compliant with plumbing, mechanical, and health codes across the jurisdictions Fluidstack builds in, and manage the permit and inspection questions that come back.

- Integrate with cooling. Work with the mechanical, water-quality, and controls engineers so make-up water, treatment, and blowdown are designed as one system with the cooling plant.

- Support the build. Review contractor submittals and shop drawings, answer RFIs, and walk installations through commissioning.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

title: Reconciliation & Payments Specialist
description:
Description
﻿Who We're Looking For - The Dream Maker
This is a hands-on reconciliation role inside Chargeflow 's Billing & Collections team . Money comes in from customers of every size - from small SMB merchants to large Enterprise accounts - across multiple payment channels, and you are the person who makes sure every payment is matched against what the customer was actually invoiced. It's detailed work, it lives largely in Excel, and getting it right matters.
The core of the job is ownership: you reconcile what a customer owes against what they've paid, you close the loop against the invoice we issued, and you don't let it go until it's genuinely resolved - including chasing an open item well after the month has closed. "It'll probably sort itself out" is not part of the role. If a customer hasn't paid their debt, you stay on it until they have.
You'll work across several systems where the data is often broken, incomplete, or simply wrong - so a critical eye is not optional. You need to be the person who notices that two numbers don't agree and cares enough to find out why. It can be frustrating, but the payoff is real: there's genuine satisfaction in untangling a mess and getting it to tie out.
We're also a company that wants to do this smarter over time. You won't be expected to build automation from day one - but we do want someone who is hungry to turn manual, repetitive work into AI-assisted workflows, with Claude as your day-to-day partner for getting there. The role sits within Billing & Collections and reports to the Billing & Collections Manager.
About Chargeflow

Chargeflow is a leading force in fintech innovation, tackling chargeback fraud and the impact it has on online businesses. Born from a deep passion for technology and eCommerce, we’ve developed an AI-driven solution that helps merchants manage credit card disputes, recover lost revenue, and protect their businesses through a unique success-based model.
Backed by $49M from Viola Growth, OpenView, Sequoia Capital, and other top-tier global investors, Chargeflow is on a product-led growth journey. We’re a tight-knit team of passionate builders and entrepreneurs, united by our mission to revolutionize eCommerce and protect online businesses from chargeback fraud.﻿
What You’ll Own
Reconciliation & Collections

• Reconcile customer payments against invoices across the full customer base - from small SMB merchants to large Enterprise accounts.

• Match every incoming payment to what the customer was actually invoiced, and close the loop between the payment received and the invoice issued.

• Investigate every unmatched, partial, or unexpected item down to root cause - don't leave gaps open.

• Track what each customer owes, confirm the debt has actually been paid, and follow up until it's fully resolved - including items that carry past month-end.

• Own your accounts end to end: you're responsible for the reconciliation being clean, correct, and complete, not just started.

• Keep clear, well-documented working papers so anyone can see how a balance was reached.

Working Across the Systems

• Do the heavy lifting in Excel - this is a spreadsheet-intensive role (pivot tables, lookups, large data sets).

• Pull and cross-check data across several systems where the data is often broken, incomplete, or inconsistent.

• Keep a critical eye at all times - assume the data needs verifying, and dig in when two numbers don't agree.

• Take real ownership of the details: notice the discrepancy, care about it, and drive it to a clean answer.

Communication & Responsiveness

• Be responsive to the people who depend on you across the company - Billing, Finance, Operations, and Customer Success.

• Work fluidly across the channels the business runs on: Slack, monday.com, and email.

• When it's the fastest way to resolve something, get on a call with a customer and walk them through their reconciliation directly.

• Explain a billing or reconciliation situation in plain, clea

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. We are seeking an experienced PeopleSoft Technical Developer to design, develop, and support customizations, integrations, and enhancements for enterprise PeopleSoft applications including HCM, FSCM, and Campus Solutions. title: Head of AI Enablement & Transformation
description:
Head of AI Enablement & Transformation
Voice Systems Engineering (VSE) is a dynamic organization driven by innovation and a shared passion for positively impacting people's lives. We operate multiple brands and businesses, including Psychic Source, Plasma Futures and Soundbed, all focused on mind and body wellbeing, with our flagship brand, Psychic Source, leading the way.
Our vision at VSE centers on the belief that when talented individuals unite, possibilities become limitless. Rooted in a remote-first environment, we've cultivated a culture that embraces diversity, equity, work-life balance, and a true sense of belonging.
For over three decades, VSE has used technology to connect people with expert, caring guidance. We are an established, profitable company, and this year we made a deliberate decision to rebuild the way we work around AI rather than simply adding it to what we already do. Many AI projects are already underway across the business, and the whole company comes together every week to focus on AI adoption. We are now looking for the person to bring that work together and lead it.
We are seeking a passionate, hands-on and experienced Head of AI Enablement & Transformation to turn that commitment into everyday practice across the company. This is a builder's role rather than an advisory one. You should be comfortable prototyping and shipping generative AI agents, automations and the tooling that lets non-engineers use them safely, and equally comfortable teaching a team of roughly forty-five people, most of them non-technical, to apply these tools in their own jobs. You will own the stack, the guardrails and the numbers. You will not have a team reporting to you; the impact of this role comes from forty-five people who can do things they could not do before, working through AI champions across the business, the tools you build and the sessions you run. VSE runs on Holacracy, and this role sits in our General Company Circle, our most senior leadership team, with clearly defined domains that are yours to decide: the tooling stack and its vendors, the skills library and agent registry, and the scorecard and its targets.
Your first priority will be consolidation rather than expansion: bringing the work already underway into one coherent, well-governed program, deciding what to standardize on and what to retire, and putting the right guardrails in place before adding anything new. For the right person, this is the part that determines whether everything that follows succeeds, and the path from this role to real company-wide impact is unusually short.
If you're our new Head of AI Enablement & Transformation, you will look forward to engaging in activities such as:

• Building and shipping AI capabilities: prototypes, agents, evaluation frameworks, and the pipeline that allows a non-engineer to deploy something safely. You will write code most weeks.

• Leading hands-on enablement across the company: a weekly working session you run, role-specific playbooks, office hours, and a network of AI champions in every function, with adoption measured in actual use rather than attendance.

• Redesigning core workflows around what AI makes possible, in partnership with the teams that do the work, rather than automating the steps that already exist.

• Owning the AI scorecard: publishing weekly results including the metrics that missed, setting targets, and being transparent when a target changes and why.

• Deciding the tooling stack: evaluating models, platforms, agent frameworks and vendors; running proofs of concept; making build-versus-buy calls; and avoiding tool sprawl.

• Building the guardrails first: a graduated autonomy model that agents earn on evidence, traceability from every output back to its prompt and approver, a permissions and data-classification model that holds, and acceptable-use policy developed with Legal, HR and IT as partners from week one.

• Managing the use-case pipeline from intake through prioritiza

title: Engineering Manager
description: At Parallel, we build AI agents to help healthcare facilities automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding. Come help us build it ! Context Parallel closed a $20M Series A with Index Ventures, is deployed in 40+ hospitals, and is scaling fast. Founders Paul Lafforgue (Polytechnique, ex-Meta, ex-McKinsey) and Chris Rydahl (who previously built Hublo, Europe's largest healthcare staffing platform) are based in Paris with the team. Our tech team is 10 people today, all reporting directly to the CTO - and it will double by 2027. A flat structure got us here, now we need managers who stay close to the code to get us there. The team is organized in streams, each run by a PM and a Stream Owner: Coding, Extraction, and Activity (activity steering, dashboarding, and our assistant products).
